newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot to set up hub in Khabarovsk.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot to set up hub in Khabarovsk.

text.p: Russian international carrier Aeroflot opened an office in Khabarovsk on Thursday as the first stage in setting up a new hub in the Russian Far East.
Gennady Danilychev, head of Aeroflot's domestic air service division, said in a statement that the carrier planned to expand its activity in this region.
"We plan to use Khabarovsk airport as a hub for our international and domestic cargo flights, including a new regular Moscow-Khabarovsk cargo route, which will be open soon," Danilychev said.

Aeroflot began regular passenger flights between Moscow and Khabarovsk in 1995 and is using Khabarovsk airport for technical stopovers by cargo aircraft flying from Europe to South East Asia and Japan.

Aeroflot spokesman Alexander Luchaninov told Reuters that the airline would begin regular domestic passenger flights from Moscow to Kaliningrad, Krasnodar, Vladikavkaz, Vladivostok, Magadan, Chelyabinsk, Yekaterinburg and Nizhny Novgorod later this year.
Last week a senior Aeroflot official said the company would not open new international routes in its summer schedule and would instead upgrade current routes.
Aeroflot makes scheduled flights from Moscow to 11 destinations in Russia and to former Soviet republics in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
"We see domestic routes as very promising and plan to develop them," he said.
Last year Aeroflot carried 3.8 million passengers compared to 3.5 million in 1995.
